messages:
maya: quick follow-up on continuous-batching: proposing a compact eviction surface focused on TRIM and COOLDOWN semantics so coordinator stays small.
sanjay: curious on TRIM semantics. does TRIM mutate an active batch or create a requeued remainder?
maya: TRIM(n_tokens) should atomically reduce batch.token_budget and return a partial result header. remainder is re-enqueued as a new batch with a new id and cooling tag. coordinator must support atomic trim CAS.
liam: how about upload/work-in-progress cost? trimming during UPLOADING might waste GPU cycles. policy should get upload_progress_pct and opt to PREEMPT_NOW vs TRIM.
jen: add billing and UX: trimmed responses yield partial status (like 206) + retry_token; billing attributes consumed tokens. we'll need telemetry fields like trim_reason and original_batch_id.
nora: cooldown prevents requeue storms. propose cooling_period_ms per-tenant after TRIM/DROP. reads as read-only by eviction.
maya: comms channel: eviction service writes decisions to lock-free ring buffer with proto.VERSION and enum actions {NOOP, TRIM, PREEMPT, DROP}. coordinator validates major version and ignores unknown enums.
sanjay: rollout: feature-flag new policy; default nodes keep legacy inline eviction. ramp to small noisy tenant first.
ops-bot: note: canary window Wed 03:00-05:00 UTC. monitor churn_ratio and preempt_rate.
liam: I'll build a microbench with Zipf tenants + kvcache locality to validate tail latency and requeue storms.
maya: thanks. i'll draft proto + small coordinator shim tomorrow and tag reviewers.
